raw_response:
I have been farming in Quzhou County for over 40 years. My family has 8 mu of good irrigated land, and I know every piece of it. I did not study much, but I know what works here. Almost everyone in my village grows winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land — that is the rotation my father did, and that is what I do. The wheat is already in the ground from last October; I sowed about 30 jin of improved seed per mu after rotary tilling the land. Now spring is here, so I will topdress the wheat with urea when it greens up, irrigate it three more times before early June, and spray for insects twice, weeds once, and wheat rust once. I expect around 1,000 jin per mu if the weather is normal. Right after harvest, I will plant maize without tilling — I buy hybrid seed from the shop every year because saved maize seed loses yield. Maize gets compound fertilizer at planting, two irrigations, two insecticide sprays, and one herbicide spray. I thought about cotton, but at my age I do not have the labor for picking it, and maize is easier. That is my plan.
